title: When will the sweet shop next give free gajak?
description: A shop gives free gajak every seven days and a visitor comes every ten days, so the free gajak is received on the first day found in both lists of days. That first shared day is called the lowest common multiple of seven and ten. Keeko doubts this and wants the shop's seventh day, when no visit happens.
teaching_notes: One idea: the next free gajak comes on the first day that is in both the shop's list and the visitor's list. Watch for students who count only the shop's days and forget that the visitor must also be at the shop.

source: The shop gives free gajak every 7 days and {{NAME_7}} visits every 10 days. After how many days does the next free gajak come?
video_script.why: The child has met common multiples with torans and now sees the same list-and-match method answer a question about days.
video_script.substitution: List the days of the shop and the days of the visits, and take the first day found in both lists.
video_script.anchor: A row of day numbers with a shop marker every 7 days and a visit marker every 10 days, the sweet shop at the left.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says free gajak comes after seven days because the shop gives it every seven days, but on day seven the visitor is not at the shop.
video_script.payoff_line: The next free gajak comes after seventy days

names.{{NAME_7}}: visits the sweet shop once every 10 days and enjoys the free gajak

never_show: day 7 as the day of the next free gajak, marked right
maths_rules: free gajak days: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70 and so on
the first day in both lists is 70, the lowest common multiple of 7 and 10
slip: on day 7 there is no visit, since 7 is not a multiple of 10
video_script.design: One idea: the first day in both lists is the day both things happen. The two day lists stay on the board from step one to the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A sweet shop gives free gajak to school children on Mondays. Gajak is a sweet made from sesame seeds, jaggery and ghee.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Today is a Monday, and {{NAME_7}} enjoyed the free gajak. {{NAME_7}} visits the shop once every ten days.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>When can {{NAME_7}} next get free gajak? Answer in number of days.

beats.on_screen: the shop and {{NAME_7}} stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a calendar strip: shop days marked in blue every 7 days, visit days marked in green every 10 days; a day with both marks is circled

marks.m1: a calendar strip of days appears
marks.m2: shop days are marked in blue, counting in sevens
marks.m3: visit days are marked in green, counting in tens
marks.m4: a day with both marks is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Imagining the days on a calendar helps us see the problem.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The shop gives free gajak every Monday, which means days counted in sevens.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The visits are counted in tens.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Free gajak is received only on a day that is in both counts.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seven, fourteen, twenty one, twenty eight, thirty five, forty two. Forty nine, fifty six, sixty three, seventy, and so on.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The next free gajak comes after seventy days.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first day in both lists is called the lowest common multiple of seven and ten.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: day 7 with a gajak; the visit list shows no visit on day 7 and the bubble is struck out; day 70 is lit again

marks.m1: Keeko's bubble shows free gajak on day 7

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks free gajak comes after seven days, because that is when the shop gives it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But on day seven, {{NAME_7}} is not at the shop.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The next visit is on day ten, so day seven does not count.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The day must be in both lists. The first such day is seventy.
